page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-capable server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 960 GB local NVMe SSD. It is also Premium Storage capable and runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth presents a notable tradeoff; read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks is weak (bottom 25%), though write bandwidth for large blocks remains average. This memory bandwidth limitation is reflected in weaker performance for memory-intensive tasks, such as software compilation with Clang and PassMark database operations, which both scored in the bottom 25%. Conversely, text processing and single-threaded operations perform well.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core and bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, the L4as_v4 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring local storage and moderate memory capacity without demanding extreme memory throughput. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 5.97 million operations per second in SET benchmarks), static web serving, and light text processing. It is less suited for memory-bandwidth-bound applications, large-scale software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where prompt processing speeds drop significantly.
